First, systemic not local: I enumerated every COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md pin in every candidate artifact in docs/coop/artifacts — 71 pins across 25 artifact families — and ALL 71 are stale against live. advisories.title: versionOrDigest is an alternation with no per-class selection rule
advisories.detail: Identity is defined as '{ class, identity, versionOrDigest }' and sameness as 'the declared name plus the declared version-or-digest'. Nothing says which classes may satisfy this by version and which must carry a digest. Two conforming TCB inventories could therefore declare the same member at different strengths.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: I attacked this as a candidate SHOULD-FIX and it does not survive, because neither branch of the alternation can land BELOW the governing law. File 04 line 162 requires an 'identity/version rule'. The version branch is exactly that floor. The digest branch is strictly stronger — bytes subsume a version label. So there is no configuration in which this alternation admits something weaker than the law demands, which is what a real hole would require. There is also a substantive reason the alternation belongs here: for genuinely system-class members that the closure does not ship — OS ABI, system libc, platform certificate store — a stable digest may not exist at all, so forcing digest-only would make the rule unsatisfiable on the very classes the row exists to cover. And per-class strength is naturally a property of populated per-OS rows, which /identityRuleShape/populatedTables reserves to DR-G22 evidence. Reserving it is the correct call, not an omission.
advisories.suggestedFix: None needed now. The G22 population act should state, per class, which strength applies — that is where the information exists.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That the subject moved during review. It did not — 89913fd8… at dispatch, at start and at end, 5799 bytes, mode 0444 throughout. I never wrote to it. It remains untracked (git status '??'), so nothing was committed either.

The dispatch's headline attack: per-OS package tables populated by fiat. REFUTED, and I looked for this the hard way rather than trusting the disclaimer. The taxonomy contains eight CLASS names and zero concrete members. There is no version string, no package name, no vendor, no platform-specific row anywhere in the artifact. The only place concrete members are even mentioned — 'which glibc, which codesign, which ICU' — is inside populatedTables, and the sentence containing them RESERVES them to DR-G22 rather than deciding them. Naming the shape of a reservation is the opposite of populating it.

That the artifact re-decides D-006's numbers. REFUTED absolutely by exhaustive scan: the artifact contains NO numeric quantities at all. Regex over the full bytes returns zero occurrences of any MB/ms/GB/% quantity, and the only multi-digit tokens in the entire file are '04' (a filename fragment) and '308' (the file 08 line number). D-006's thresholds cannot be re-decided by a document that states no numbers. Conversely, D-006 clause 2 is the affirmative authority FOR this row: 'DR-G02 (installed core/TCB): immutable installed tree ≤ 80 MB; mandatory-closure inventory enumerated, zero undeclared dependencies (the qualitative half is DR-126's).' The artifact takes the qualitative half and leaves the number where D-006 put it.

That the artifact re-owns DR-G07 extraction. REFUTED on scope and on bytes. The artifact confines itself to file 04 lines 161-166 and its surroundingLaw states extraction/symlink/TOCTOU/spawn-binding remain DR-G07 / DR-103. I verified the section boundary independently: 'Exact-byte delivery' is the heading at line 141, the next heading ('Separate compatibility matrices') is at 168, line 167 is blank — so the section is L141-166 exactly as the artifact claims, and 161-166 is genuinely its final paragraph, not a slice cut to flatter the row. The artifact carries no extraction, archive, traversal, symlink, hard-link, sparse, case-folding or TOCTOU rule. It does not touch the L143-155 successor-binding list or the L157-159 DR-G07 sentence.

That ambient or undeclared system resolution is anywhere treated as lawful. REFUTED. Every mention is a refusal. /identityRuleShape/refuse enumerates four: undeclared library/framework/tool resolution, alternate loader search, identity drift, and ambient PATH / system-runtime / install-time substitution. NT-TCB-4 puts a hostile clean machine behind the ambient case. There is no exception clause, no waiver path, no 'unless', and no escape hatch anywhere in the object — I checked for the inert-exception pattern specifically, since that is where this kind of artifact leaks.

That refuse[3] quietly annexes the whole file 04 substitution bullet. REFUTED as an over-reach and confirmed as a deliberate split. Line 152-153 forbids 'PATH, loader, shell, live-project, system-runtime, or install-time substitution'. The artifact claims PATH, system-runtime and install-time; drops shell and live-project (which are spawn/project-resolution territory, not TCB); and handles loader separately at refuse[1] as alternate loader search. It labels the source and hedges in its own bytes — 'file 04 exact-byte list; this row owns the TCB half'. That is a correct partition, not an annexation.

That SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, DEMONSTRATED, a seal, or an implementation authorization slipped in. REFUTED by enumerating every occurrence in the bytes. SATISFIED × 1 — inside a reviewGuidance instruction to attack such claims. QUALIFIED × 2 — one is /g22/doesNotClaim, a denial; one is the same attack instruction. 'Does not SATISFY DR-126' appears as an explicit denial conditioned on 'a later D-000 MF-6'. DEMONSTRATED × 0. AUTHORIZ × 0. 'docs/v2/implementation/' × 2, both denials. Header discipline is correct and complete: CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING.

That the MF-6 reference is decoration. REFUTED — it is load-bearing and accurate. COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md line 256 establishes 'Register-content changes are DECISIONS, not hygiene (MF-6)', and line 1719 confirms file-08 amendments route through MF-6. The artifact's claim that DR-126's status moves only via a later D-000 MF-6 is exactly the corpus rule, cited correctly.

All eight terms appear in the governing sentence, in the law's own order (character offsets strictly ascending), with nothing added and nothing dropped — including the awkward trailing 'comparable system-class dependency', which a drafter trimming to look tidier would have been tempted to lose.

The artifact's slice1 list matches on all four, and its 'windows: DELIBERATELY absent. D-002.' matches the recorded deferral. It cites the owner rather than re-deciding.

'Absence of a retained trace is a failed qualification, not a silent pass' is the analytic consequence of file 04's 'Loader traces are retained at qualification' being a requirement — an unmet requirement failing is what a requirement means, not a new decision. verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 4 advisories. The dispatch gate was 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. ACCEPT.
verdictStatement: I went after this on every line the dispatch named and on four of my own, and it holds. The three verbatim carries are byte-exact under equality tests rather than inspection — the six TCB lines against file 04 161-166, the register row against file 08 line 308, and the taxonomy against the law's own sentence in the law's own order, trailing awkward class included. Both source digests that matter MATCH live. The row anchor resolves uniquely: '| DR-126 |' occurs exactly once in the register. The document's discipline is where a candidate like this usually fails, and it does not fail. It states no numbers at all — not one quantity in 5799 bytes — so D-006's thresholds are untouchable from here, while D-006 clause 2 affirmatively hands this row the qualitative half in its own words. It populates no per-OS row; the only concrete members it mentions are named inside the sentence that reserves them to DR-G22. It confines itself to the section's final paragraph, verified by locating the section boundaries myself, and leaves extraction, symlinks and TOCTOU with DR-G07. Its harness id is not coined but copied from file 08 line 356, standing and non-claim intact — which was my strongest available attack, given how often this corpus has parked harness naming as CONTESTED, and it is shut. Every mention of ambient or undeclared resolution is a refusal, with no exception clause anywhere. The four advisories are real but none is chargeable. The stale COORDINATOR-DECISIONS pin is the only one that tempted me toward SHOULD-FIX, and it does not survive contact with the evidence: it was exact on the artifact's own authoring date, all 71 such pins in the corpus are stale including accepted-at-0/0 artifacts, the intervening commits touch other rows entirely, and — decisively — I tested the two claims it secures against the live file instead of the pin, and both hold. Charging it here would be inventing a standard and applying it to one row retroactively. The versionOrDigest alternation was my second candidate and fails for a cleaner reason: neither branch can land below file 04's 'identity/version' floor, so it admits nothing weaker than the law, and per-class strength is properly G22's to pin. This artifact does the narrow thing it says it does and declines the six larger things it could have taken.

coordinatorNote: ACCEPT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-126 stays OPEN at file 08 line 308; I did not touch file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, did not mark anything SATISFIED, did not authorize docs/v2/implementation/, and did not commit. Four things to weigh. First, this is a genuinely narrow candidate: it locks the qualitative TCB shape D-006 clause 2 explicitly left to this row, and reserves the per-OS tables to DR-G22 rather than inventing them — so accepting it closes no evidence obligation and the row's real work stays at qualification. Second, my four advisories are all carryable; none needs a v2, and ADV-1 in particular is a corpus-wide convention question (all 71 COORDINATOR-DECISIONS pins in docs/coop/artifacts are stale against live) that should not be settled on DR-126's back — if the coordinator wants it fixed, fix the convention, not this file. Third, an independence note: the Codex verdict file appeared on disk partway through my review and I measured it (fd054d3a…, 3495 bytes) without opening it, so the two lanes are uncorrelated — if the lanes disagree, that disagreement is real signal rather than one reviewer having read the other. Fourth, one drafting observation for whoever authors the G22 population act: it will need to state, per class, whether version or digest is the required identity strength (ADV-3), since the shape here permits both and the information to choose only exists at population time.
